summary: Ghost Rovers & Cosmic Relics is an interactive educational website aimed at showing school children passionate about space the historic NASA spacecraft, rovers, landers and equipment that have been abandoned on the Moon, Mars and far off in space since the 1960s. Moving away from heavy books Ghost Rovers & Cosmic Relics brings to life old landmarks and far off probes like Apollo 11's Eagle, Opportunity, InSight and Voyager 1 with vibrant illustrations, interactive planetary maps and first person storytelling. Young explorers can learn about the science these machines did, create their own spacecraft in an interactive engineering lab to understand how power sources and equipment make up a mission and earn badges for missions by answering space trivia. As a standalone website built using HTML, CSS and JavaScript Ghost Rovers & Cosmic Relics uses fictional retro space sounds to make the distant engineering history fun and creative allowing old robot pioneers to connect to new discoveries.
details: Ghost Rovers & Cosmic Relics is a lively, interactive educational web app that introduces children aged 7–14 to historic NASA spacecraft, rovers, and instruments left behind across the Moon, Mars, and deep space since the 1960s. Users navigate illustrated celestial maps to hear first-person stories from famous hardware such as Apollo 11's Eagle, Opportunity, InSight, and Voyager 1, build custom spacecraft in a Build-a-Rover Engineering Lab, and collect digital badges through a space trivia quiz. Created with HTML5, CSS3 (Tailwind CSS), JavaScript, custom inline SVG artwork, and procedural Web Audio sound effects, the project turns dense aerospace history into an imaginative, accessible STEM adventure that links past robotic pioneers to today's discoveries.
